Directions:Study the following information carefully and answer the questions accordingly.

In a certain code language

“stop around social media” is written as “zi sa cp hn”

“much media reacts like” is written as “mb cp wv pd”

questions.explanation:
around = sa
social = zi
media = cp
much = mb
post = tk
stop = hn
his = ol
get / director = fg / re
reacts / like = wv / pd

questions.question: Which of the following is second letter from the left end of the meaningful word formed by the 3rd, 5th, 6th, and 9th letter of the word “FURNITURE”. If more than one word is formed mark X as your answer. If no such word is formed mark Y as your answer?
questions.explanation:
The word is "FURNITURE".
Let's identify the letters at the given positions:

3rd letter: R

5th letter: I

6th letter: T

9th letter: E

The letters are R, I, T, E.

Check meaningful words that can be formed using these letters:

"RITE" (meaningful)

"TIRE" (meaningful)

"Tier" (meaningful)

Since more than one meaningful word is possible, the answer is "X".
Hence, the correct ans is "X".

Directions:Study the following information carefully and answer the questions given below:

 

Eight persons J, K, L, M, N, O, P and Q went to a bank to open a savings account. They filled the form and it was noted that each of them was born on the same date i.e. on 28th January but in different years. The years were 1959, 1966, 1967, 1972, 1976, 1983, 1992 and 1999 not necessarily in the same order. Make the calculations as on 28th January 2022.
P was 16 years elder to N. Number of persons born after N was twice as that of the number of persons born before J. N was not the youngest. Q was born after 1969 but before 1994. Two persons were born between Q and O. Q was elder to O. Number of persons born before K was two more than the number of persons born after L. At least one person was born between K and P.

 

How many persons were born between O and L?
questions.explanation:
Their age as on 28rd January will be:

- P was 16 years elder to N. The possible cases are (55, 39) (46, 30) (39, 23). As N was not the youngest (39, 23) will be invalid.

- Number of persons born after N was twice as that of the number of persons born before J. Thus, case 2 becomes invalid.

- Q was born after 1969 but before 1994

- 2 persons were born between Q and O. Q was elder to O.

- Number of persons born before K was 2 more than the number of persons born after L. 

- At least one person was born between K and P. 

The final table will be as follows:

Three persons were born between O and L.

Eight people, A, B, C, D, E, F, G and H, are seated around an octagonal table, with one at each side of the table. All are facing the centre.
G sits second to the right of H. E sits second to the right of F, who is adjacent to D. C sits third to the right of B. A sits immediate left of D. H is an immediate neighbour of C.

 

How many people are there between E and D, when counted clockwise from E?
questions.explanation:
A sits immediate left of D.

E sits second to the right of F, who is adjacent to D.

C sits third to the right of B.

H is an immediate neighbour of C.

G sits second to the right of H.

Therefore, this is the final arrangement.

Two people are there between E and D, when counted clockwise from E.

questions.question: A wire is looped in the form of a rectangle whose area is 1200 cm2 and the ratio of length to breadth of the rectangle is 4:3. If the same wire is looped in the form of a circle, what is the area of the circle?
questions.explanation:
Let length & breadth of the rectangle be 4x & 3x cm respectively.

Area \(= \ 1200\ \)

\(= > 4x \times 3x = 1200\)

\(= > x^{2} = 100\)

\(= > x\  = \ 10\ \)

Therefore; \(length\  = \ 40\ cm\ \&\ breadth\  = \ 30\ cm\)

So; Perimeter of rectangle will be equal to perimeter of circle when looped in a circle.

\(= > 2 \times \frac{22}{7} \times r\  = \ 2(40 + 30)\)

\(= > \ \frac{22}{7} \times r = 70\)

\(= > \ r\  = \ \frac{245}{11}\text{cm}\)

Area of circle = \(\pi r^{2} = \ \frac{22}{7} \times (\frac{245}{11})^{2} = \frac{120050}{77} = \frac{17150}{11}cm^{2}\)

Gold in mixture alloy = 513 × 195 = 75

∴ The ratio is 3:10

questions.question: Krishna, Mahesh and Gautam can do a work in 90, 30 and 45 days respectively. If they work together, in how many days will they complete work?
questions.explanation:
Calculation:

Krishna’s one day’s work = \(\frac{1}{90}\)

Mahesh’s one day’s work = \(\frac{1}{30}\)

gautam’s one day’s work = \(\frac{1}{45}\)

Krishna, Mahesh and gautam together can do the work = \(\frac{1}{90} + \frac{1}{30} + \frac{1}{45} = \ \frac{1}{90}(1 + 3 + 2) = \frac{6}{90} = \frac{1}{15}\)

So, they will complete the work in 15 days.

Alternate Method:

LCM of 90, 30, and 45 is 90.

Therefore, Total work = 90

Krishna :  90                  1

Mahesh : 30        90      3

Gautam : 45                  2

The efficiency of Krishna, Mahesh, and Gautam is 1, 3, and 2, respectively.

Total days required to complete the work = 90/6 = 15 days

questions.explanation:
Upstream time is 5 hours and downstream time is 3 hours.

So, the ratio of the speed of Pawan and stream = =12d3+d5:12d3-d5 = 4:1.

Let the speed of Pawan be 4k km/hr in still water and the speed of the hat be k km/hr

Distance of point X = 4k+k×3 = 15k km

Time taken by hat cover 15k km = 15kk=15 hours

So that will reach at 6 PM.

questions.question: 'A' and 'B' started a business together by investing in ratio x:(x + 3). Six months later, 'A' doubled his investment. If at the end of the year, the profit earned by 'A' is Rs. 3,600 out of total profit of Rs. 7,800, then find the value of 'x'.
questions.explanation:
Let the amount invested by 'A' and 'B' be Rs. 'xy' and Rs. (x + 3)y

Profit earned by 'B' = 7800 - 3600 = Rs. 4,200

Ratio of profit shares of 'A' and 'B' = (6xy + 12xy) : {(x + 3) X 12y} = 18xy:(12xy + 36y)

ATQ;

{18xy/(12xy + 36y)} = (3600/4200) = (6/7)

Or, 18xy X 7 = 6 X (12xy + 36y)

Or, 7x = 4x + 12

Or, 3x = 12

So, x = 4

Hence, option d.

questions.question: $45 is contained in a box.The box has $1,￠50 and ￠25 coins in the ratio of 2:3:4. Find the total number of ￠25 and ￠50 coins.(1$ = 100￠)
questions.explanation:
Given, ratio of $1,￠50 and ￠25 coins = 2:3:4

So, total money of 1 unit of ratio = $(2\(\times 1\)) + ￠(50\(\times\)3) + ￠(25\(\times\)4)

= $ 2 + ￠250

= $ 2 + $ 2.5

= $ 4.5

So, total units = \(\frac{45}{4.5}\) = 10 units

As, 1 unit has three ￠50 & four￠25 coins

So, 10 units will have = 3\(\times\) 10 = 30 ￠50 coins

And, 10 units will have = 4\(\times\) 10 = 40 ￠25 coins

So, total number of coins of ￠50 coins & ￠25 coins = 30 + 40 = 70

questions.question: 0.5 decade ago, Laxmi was quadrice as old as her daughter Priya. 0.8 decades hence, Laxmi’s age will beat her daughter’s age by 1.2 decades. The proportion of the current ages of Laxmi and Priya is :
questions.explanation:
Let, Ages of Laxmi and Priya 5 years ago was 4A and A years correspondingly.

Then current age of Laxmi and Priya is (4A + 5) & (A + 5)
Then according to question,

[(4A + 5) + 8] – [(A + 5) + 8] = 12

(4A + 13) – (A + 13) = 12
4A + 13 – A – 13 = 12

3A = 12

=> A = 4

Required Ratio = (4A +5) : (A + 5) = 21 : 9

= 7 : 3

questions.question: 20 students appear in a test. Average of marks obtained in the test by them is 78. If due to typing mistake, the marks of one student was printed 36 instead of 63 then what is the correct average of the marks obtained by them?
questions.explanation:
Total marks obtained by the 20 students \(= 78 \times 20 = 1560\)

Correct total marks will be \(= 1560 - 36 + 63 = 1587\)

Correct average is \(= \frac{1587}{20} = 79.35\)

questions.question: 1500 rupees is invested in scheme A at R% p.a. simple interest. Another amount (1500 - x) is invested in scheme B at 2R % p.a. simple interest. After four years, interest earned from scheme A is 25% less than that of scheme B. Find x.
questions.explanation:
Interest earned from scheme A = \(\frac{1500 \times R \times 4}{100} = 60R\)

Interest earned from scheme B = \(\frac{\left( 1500 - x \right) \times 2R \times 4}{100} = \frac{2R\left( 1500 - x \right)}{25}\)

According to Question,

\(60R\  = \ \frac{3}{4} \times \frac{2R\left( 1500 - x \right)}{25}\)

\(1500 - x\  = 1000\)

\(\Rightarrow x = 500\)

∴ The answer is 500.

\(? = \left( \frac{? + 65}{216} \right) \times 72 \times \frac{1}{35} \times 840 \times \frac{1}{18}\)

\(\Rightarrow \ ? = \left( ? + \ 65 \right) \times \frac{4}{9}\)

⇒ 9 × ? = 4 × ? + 260

⇒ 5 × ? = 260

? = 52
